tm_config.hardware: Trained with TMU (Python). Inference: C++ (T1 vanilla: byte include flags per literal; T2: 16-bit indices of included literals only, after REDRESS [11]) cross-compiled with the RISC-V GNU toolchain, run on the UltraEmbedded single-core 5-stage RV32IM+Zicsr core (R1, 59 instructions, 14 ns clock) and the reduced core (R2, 27 instructions, no MUL/DIV, 12 ns clock), both with AXI tightly coupled IMEM/DMEM, synthesized and simulated in Xilinx Vivado targeting a Zynq-7000 ZC702 (not run on the board). Table II gives one accuracy per clause count; the paper does not say whether it was computed on the RISC-V simulation or in TMU software.

notes: Hardware paper: TMs trained in TMU, inference in C++ on two RISC-V soft cores (R1 full RV32IM, R2 reduced 27-instruction) synthesized and simulated in Vivado for a Zynq-7000 ZC702; nothing is measured on the board (power from Vivado, time = cycles x clock period, energy = P x T). Table II accuracies have no statement of whether they come from the RISC-V simulation or TMU; T2 is stated to be functionally equivalent to T1, but the record's per-row note that accuracy is 'identical for T1/T2 and R1/R2' is a reading of the single Table II value, not an explicit sentence. Per-dataset execution time and energy are only in log-scale Figs. 5-6 (not extracted). Abstract says execution time reduced 'by up to 98%' (also Sec. V) while Sec. IV says maximum 99.28%; the record follows Sec. IV. Table III percentages are internally inconsistent for R1 FF (2393/106400 printed as 4.70%) and R1 DSP (4/200 printed as 1.82%); raw counts are used in the record. Fig. 3: T2 cuts ADD/ADDI/LW/SW instruction counts by 96.3-97.7% (not a record result). No train/test split, seeds, T or s given. Modality/domain of the UCI sets chosen from Table I descriptions (Gesture and EMG as time_series like other sidecars).
